newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate down to 11.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate down to 11.8 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate edged down to 11.8 percent from 12.2 percent on Monday, amid an abundant supply of kuna funds, delears said.
They said demand at 54.6 million kuna was met in full, leaving a surplus of 45.4 million on the supply side. Fresh borrowings accounted for 30.6 million.
More than half of new loans were call money at a steady rate of 11 percent. Two short-term placements were made at 12 and 15 percent and one two-month loan was struck at 16 percent.
Insurers charged a steady 9.0 percent for old loans. Banks rolled over previous funds at rates ranging between 11 percent for call money and 15 percent for term loans.
The central bank calculated its kuna mid rates for Tuesday at 5.5396 against the dollar and 3.5622 against the mark. -- Laura Lui, Zareb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
